description: The trace-invisible 7.67 % of epsNPq lives in the traceless part of the 2-dimensional block, and survives the convention-D Temperley-Lieb quotient intact.

assertion_notes.note: (e_(3) and e_(1,1,1) annihilate [H,H]; e_(2,1) acts as the identity)
(so Delta's (2,1) part is TRACELESS — the same fact as chi^(2,1)(Delta) = 0, found separately and now unified)
(D quotients the (1,1,1) block; dC is in (2,1), so the trace-invisible remainder is NOT what D removes — qou-xzrj stays live under the canonical convention)
(so -h*y_(2,1)(1) is not a coincidence of labels: it is the weight of the very block the remainder lives in)

data.verdict: The trace-invisible remainder lives in the TRACELESS part of the 2-dimensional block, and this unifies four facts that arrived separately. For H_3 = R + M_2 + R the commutator subspace is sl_1 + sl_2 + sl_1 = sl_2, so [H,H] sits ENTIRELY in the (2,1) block (measured: the two 1-dim idempotents annihilate it, e_(2,1) is the identity on it, dim = 3). Hence dC is in that block; Delta's (2,1)-component IS dC exactly, which is the SAME statement as chi^(2,1)(Delta) = 0; and the floor -h*y_(2,1)(1) carries that block's own weight rather than coincidentally sharing its label. So Delta splits as two 1-dimensional blocks carrying everything a trace can see, plus a traceless element of the 2-dimensional block carrying everything it cannot. AND THE URGENT QUESTION: convention D quotients the (1,1,1) block, dC is in (2,1), so the remainder SURVIVES the Temperley-Lieb quotient intact -- it is not what D removes, and qou-xzrj stays live under the canonical convention. NOT claimed: that anything in the framework's vocabulary evaluates a traceless element of a 2-dimensional block. That is what remains open; this says where to look.
